declared_against.note: RECORDS, NOT DEPENDENCES.  These shas say which state of the subject the values below were read from.  Nothing in this gate resolves them, and this directory DECLARES NO DEPENDENCE ON THEIR REACHABILITY (mg-223d's convention: 87 directories mention reachability, 0 declared a dependence on it, and the difference is what makes a pin a pin).  If they are pruned, this file is a slightly less useful record and the gate is unaffected.  mg-188d re-read every value below against both suites after reconciling ledger row 8; the six moved fields carry their reason in their own `why` and the shas above are the states mg-724a read, left as the record they are.

how_to_move_a_value: By hand, in the same commit as the change that moved it, with the reason written into that field's `why`.  There is deliberately NO --refresh mode in gate.py: a gate that can rewrite its own expectations on demand converts every red into a keystroke, which is laundering with extra steps.

twin.runner_exit.why: code/rendered_twin_pin_9bc2/run_all.sh exits 0 ON DRIFT, deliberately — its own header says drift is the normal condition of a hand-maintained rendering between reconciliations.  Gated at 0 so that a change to 2 (structural failure, or a hole found by its negative control) is red, and so that a change to a different mapping shows up here rather than nowhere.

twin.control_exit.why: twin_pin.py finds no drift (0).  MOVED 1 -> 0 BY mg-188d, WHICH RECONCILED ROW 8 — the event the previous `why` named as the only legitimate reason for this number to move, and the row it named.  The reconciliation is a rewritten row-8 cell in the twin's ledger plus a re-pin in the same commit; the pin records that the cell WAS updated and cannot verify it, so the diff is the evidence (mg-9bc2 COVERAGE.md §4).  A move back to 1 means a published ledger row has moved away from its rendered twin, which is what this gate is for.  It no longer moves on a STATE.md edit OUTSIDE the ledger: section 3 stopped grading at mg-188d, for the reason written into twin_pin.py beside the change and measured there.

twin.negative_exit.why: 0 means every one of negative_control.py's mutations was caught by the section that claimed it.  Anything else is a hole in the twin's control, which mg-9bc2's runner calls worse than drift.

twin.verdict_grade.why: The grade word out of twin_pin.py's own VERDICT line, read via the runner's `control verdict:` echo so the pattern matches once.  MOVED "DRIFT" -> "CLEAN" by mg-188d: the previous `why` said CLEAN would mean row 8 was reconciled and that this is a real event that should move this file.  It was, and it did.

twin.worklist.why: THE FIELD THIS GATE EXISTS FOR.  The suite's exit code is 0 whether this list is [] or [7, 8] or [1, 2, 7, 8], so a gate reading the exit code cannot see a published ledger row moving away from its rendered twin.  Read as a SET so that ordering is not a verdict.  MOVED ["8"] -> [] by mg-188d, which reconciled row 8 — the second drifted row that no ticket named until this one.  TWO THINGS HAD TO CHANGE FOR AN EMPTY LIST TO BE READABLE AT ALL, and both are mg-188d's: the twin runner printed this line ONLY in its DRIFT branch, so the field existed exactly while the twin was broken and vanished when it was fixed — the first clean twin in that page's history took this gate to REFUSED (exit 2) and blocked the merge saying the GATE was broken rather than that the twin was clean, measured before it was fixed.  The runner now prints the line on every run and lib724a reads `(none)` as the empty set.

twin.mutations_caught.why: 16 of 16 mutations caught by negative_control.py.  A drop means the twin's control has gone blind to something it used to see.

twin.mutations_total.why: The number of mutations negative_control.py plants.  Gated because a mutation quietly deleted is coverage quietly removed, and it would otherwise be invisible: 15 of 15 caught reads exactly like 16 of 16.

twin.holes.why: Mutations the section that claimed them did not catch.

twin.unfalsifiable_rows.why: mg-9876's generalised guard: rows whose expect string is already present in the UNMUTATED report, i.e. probes that cannot fail.  This is the counter that would have caught `"8 9" in out` for its whole life.

audit.runner_exit.why: code/control_audit_9876/run_all.sh exits 0.  MOVED 1 -> 0 BY mg-188d, AND THE REASON IS THE ONE THE PREVIOUS `why` DEMANDED: arm C3 WAS REPAIRED, not silenced — a2's C3 now re-points the sandbox pin's `state-sha256` at the sandbox's own STATE.md so its predicate is false on the good input, which is C2's own documented rule applied to the arm it had not been applied to.  A move back to 1 means the audit found something; read out_a2_discriminate.txt rather than moving this number.

audit.broken_producers.why: Producers that exited without printing their own decision line.  Non-zero means a run did not reach a verdict, which mg-9876 established is not the same as finding nothing.

audit.producers_with_findings.why: Producers of code/control_audit_9876 that ended with a finding.  MOVED 1 -> 0 by mg-188d: the one producer with a finding was a2, and its finding was arm C3 scored UNFALSIFIABLE, which mg-188d repaired (see audit.runner_exit).  Gated in both directions: 1 or more means something new is red — read the transcript rather than moving this number; 0 -> anything requires the same reading in reverse.

audit.census_grade.why: a1's machine completeness check: the hand registry covers every arm-shaped site it rediscovers in code/rendered_twin_pin_9bc2.  INCOMPLETE means arms were added there and not registered — it fired for real during mg-9876 when that ticket's own repairs added 13.

audit.arms.why: Registered arms.  a1's scope is code/rendered_twin_pin_9bc2 ONLY, so this number does not move when other tickets add directories — which is what makes it gateable where the sweep counts below are not.

audit.sites.why: Arm-shaped sites the census rediscovers in that same bounded directory.

audit.arms_probed.why: Arms a2 ran against a known-bad input.  Must track audit.arms; a gap between them means arms exist that nothing tried to falsify.

audit.arms_discriminating.why: Arms demonstrated RED against a known-bad input and silent on the good one.  MOVED 49 -> 50 by mg-188d's repair of C3 (see audit.runner_exit).  RED IS EITHER DIRECTION: 50 -> 49 means an arm stopped discriminating; 50 -> 51 means an arm was added and the census must move with it.

audit.arms_not_shown.why: Arms scored UNFALSIFIABLE — predicate already true on the GOOD input.  MOVED 1 -> 0 by mg-188d, and the previous `why` asked for exactly this: gated at 1 so that C3's repair would be a deliberate, reviewable act rather than a number that quietly becomes 0.  IT IS GATED AT 0 AND NOT RECLASSIFIED AS RECORDED, WHICH WAS THE OTHER OPTION AND IS WORTH SAYING: mg-188d's reconciliation made C3 discriminate BY ACCIDENT — STATE.md happened to be byte-identical to the pin — and 0 would then have been a dated reading about whether the corpus was still, red at the next unrelated STATE.md edit, i.e. the `fails for reasons the author cannot act on` mode this file's own recorded/gated split exists to avoid.  So C3's good side was repaired instead, and 0 was DEMONSTRATED stable by re-running the audit against a STATE.md with a line appended: 50 of 50 either way.  Also affected R1-R4, whose good side borrowed a drifted row from the live tree and came back SETUP FAILED the moment the tree was clean — four arms of the auditor destroyed by the subject being fixed, the third time a fixture in this lineage borrowed the subject's own brokenness.

audit.aux_holes.why: Auxiliary defects still CONFIRMED — arms that discriminate but are blind to a specific bad input their name promises to catch.  All six mg-9876 found were repaired.

audit.selftest_scored.why: Planted worlds in which the auditor returned the known verdict.  a3 scored 7 arms red on its FIRST run of which six were defects in its own probes, so this counter is the one mg-9876 says to read first.

audit.selftest_total.why: Planted worlds a3 plants.  Gated for the same reason as twin.mutations_total: 5 of 5 reads exactly like 6 of 6.

audit.sweep_grade.why: a4's own two-sided control answered both ways.  BROKEN means the sweep's detector stopped discriminating, at which point its counts below are not citable — so the GRADE is gated even though the counts are not.

audit.sweep_membership_candidates.why: RECORDED, NOT GATED, and this is a deliberate blind spot rather than an omission.  A RECORDED VALUE IS A DATED READING AND IS EXPECTED TO GO STALE; a GATED value is an expectation and is not.  That difference is the whole of the class distinction.  a4 sweeps EVERY directory under code/, so this count moves when any ticket adds code — and the gate runs on the REBASED tree, so it moves when SOMEBODY ELSE's branch lands.  MEASURED, on the first live run: 206 in this worktree and 207 in the refinery, because code/dated_population_2ff6 landed on main while mg-724a was being written.  Had this field been gated, mg-724a's own branch would have been blocked by an unrelated merge — the exact `a gate that fails for reasons the author cannot act on` failure mode, arriving on the first run rather than in six weeks.  This directory itself adds ZERO whole-output membership tests, which is mg-9876's own detector reporting on the instrument written to gate it.

audit.sweep_tee_sites.why: Same population and same reasoning as audit.sweep_membership_candidates.  18 of these were live when mg-9876 measured; the count is a candidate index, not an adjudication.

audit.sweep_dirs_without_evidence.why: Directories under code/ shipping code with no evidence of any falsification attempt.  Same population and same reasoning; this is the number that should go DOWN as the estate is widened past these two directories, and watching it is the point of recording it.  IT WENT UP TO 26 DURING mg-724a AND THE 26TH WAS THIS DIRECTORY — a4 looks for a SOURCE FILE named for a negative/self/positive control, and this gate's falsification originally lived inside gate.py where no filename said so.  The transcript that does carry the red tokens is the one the run is still writing when a4 reads it, which is mg-f8e5's d5 defect committed by the instrument reporting it.  Repaired by moving the probes into negative_control.py — a rename that follows the estate's convention instead of arguing with the detector.
